target.title: feat: show cloud workspace conflicts in the Control UI
target.body:
Related: #110224 (phase 3 of 3; phases 1 and 2 were #110952 and #111244)

## What

Completes the operator-facing recovery path for cloud workspace conflicts. The Control UI now renders the phase-2 conflict projection as warning sidebar badges and a dismissible chat notice with the affected paths, staged-result ref, and copyable inspect/take-cloud commands. The durable `cloud-workspace-conflict` transcript entry renders as a structured event after the live notice is cleared.

The current version also keeps conflicts discoverable through collapsed session trees, reclaimed placements, and child-session rows. Display-safe paths remain visible even when their contents are not safe to interpolate into a terminal command; generated Git commands use only structurally valid, shell-safe paths and are withheld otherwise.

## Why

The Gateway already keeps local versions, applies non-conflicting cloud changes, preserves the cloud result under a staged Git ref, and records the conflict in the session. Before this change, that recovery state was hidden in raw placement and transcript data. Operators need an explicit explanation and deliberate recovery controls instead of a blind retry.

This phase adds no protocol or persistence shape. It consumes the landed phase-2 `workspaceResultConflict` projection and `cloud-workspace-conflict` transcript details with `paths`, `stagedResultRef`, and `totalCount`.

## User Impact

Operators can see that a cloud turn completed with workspace conflicts, identify which local paths were kept, inspect the staged cloud version, and deliberately take that version when appropriate. Non-conflicting cloud changes remain applied. Conflict status stays visible on the owning session and collapsed ancestors, while durable transcript history survives notice dismissal and reload.

## Evidence

- Focused Control UI proof at head `872b89e1bcd5ae29c8153102940f9823d8b62e66`: 4 files passed, 447 tests passed (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts ui/src/components/session-row-badges.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.ts`).
- Exact-head hosted CI is green, including `openclaw/ci-gate`: [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29686281202).
- Structured AutoReview (`--mode branch --base origin/main`, Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`) is clean on the exact head, with no accepted/actionable findings and overall verdict `patch is correct` (0.91 confidence).
- Conflict-specific browser lifecycle proof on a synced Blacksmith Testbox: 1 test passed in 2.53s. It rendered the live notice and sidebar badge, dismissed the notice while retaining structured history, reloaded the cleared session, and confirmed the badge and notice stayed absent while the durable history card remained. The three screenshot SHA-256 prefixes were `1518bb3a`, `a749df9b`, and `e7c91a4d`. This proof uses a mocked Gateway state and is supplemental rather than real cloud-worker evidence. [Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29684690662)
- Mantis exercised the candidate Control UI browser shell and published its generic chat screenshot and recording. This is also supplemental browser-environment evidence. [Mantis artifacts](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/web-ui-chat-proof/pr-111329/run-29684136714-1/index.json)
- Real-boundary attempt: an isolated exact-head Gateway created a real managed workspace and session, but every available worker backend failed before allocating a lease. The brokered AWS path rejected its expired authorization, direct AWS had no usable credentials, the Testbox backend timed out, the local container engine was unavailable, and the arm64 VM warmup timed out. Provider inventories confirmed that no worker lease was created, so this PR does not claim a successful real cloud-worker conflict turn.
- The rebase retained current-main inline approval cards and approval badges while adding the conflict UI. The landed phase-2 contract names did not require translation.

AI-assisted: yes. The rebased diff was reviewed and validated before publication.
